commit_scope: Release request telemetry's provider-refresh lock dependency at the source of pulse latency and proxy withdrawal.
evidence_refs: Before repair, unchanged deployed image b2326c331e845f87278cdfe6e3c01a620084e109 repeatedly became unhealthy: Docker ping exceeded its existing 5-second deadline, and public routes returned the proxy's 404 page not found.

Two live stack observations found MainThread in automation_usage_service.invalidate_cache line 59, called by runtime_service._invalidate_runtime_events_cache -> record_event -> capture_runtime_metrics. Provider refresh workers owned or waited for the same lock during collect_usage_overview. The request event loop therefore waited on unrelated provider collection, including liveness traffic.

Removed the unconditional cross-service full-cache flush from both runtime event writers and the redundant second assignment. Runtime event caches still invalidate; provider caches retain their existing refresh, expiry and explicit invalidation. No lock widening, timeout relaxation or health-check bypass.

pulse_latency_trace.bml runs one parallel, source-owned HTTP observation wave on fkwu, retaining bodies and headers privately and emitting transport exit, HTTP status, DNS/connect/TLS/first-byte/total timings and the serving runtime header. The first wave reproduced public 404s in 162-175ms, while web was 478ms and pulse 2096ms.
No fkwu/kernel source changed and no kernel or application suite ran. The only host-code change is deletion. New diagnostic logic is BML; production recovery and route readings follow deployment.

local_validation.summary: Direct native observation, two production stacks and source diff; no suite.
